payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are the scene's tonal modeling and reflections represented as pencil-drawn shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
node.criteria: Pass if pencil-rendered tonal values broadly convey the scene's volume, lighting and reflective surfaces through stroke density, hatching, form-following graphite marks or convincing rubbed graphite tones. Smooth shading can satisfy this condition when it visibly reads as graphite rendering. Isolated imperfect surfaces do not require failure. Fail if substantial surfaces retain photographic gradients, realistic specular reflections or photographic tonal modeling underneath added grain or strokes. Pencil-like surface marks, stronger outlines and desaturation alone do not satisfy this tonal-modeling condition. Assess tonal representation independently of contour linework and the mere presence of surface marks. Use unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to establish the tonal-rendering style.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the instruction to change the image into pencil drawing. Independently judge this tonal-rendering condition as pass, fail or unknown. Inspect the pitcher and wine glass gradients and highlights, the volume modeling of sprouts and carrots, and shaded food, plate and table surfaces. Determine whether the tonal transitions and reflections themselves broadly read as graphite-rendered values or remain photographic beneath added texture. Cite concrete regions and the visible shading characteristics supporting that distinction. Stroke-density modeling, hatching, form-following marks and convincing rubbed graphite tones can establish pencil shading; smooth transitions and preserved lighting geometry alone cannot establish retained photography, since smooth graphite rendering is allowed. Conversely, surface speckling, desaturation and contour changes alone cannot establish converted tonal modeling. Assess the breadth of pencil-rendered modeling across the scene without requiring every highlight or isolated surface to be perfect. Use unknown only when the visual evidence cannot establish tonal-rendering style, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is desaturated and has fine grain and softened outlines, but the pitcher and wine glass retain smooth, photographic-looking gradients and highlights. The sprouts, carrots, roasted food, plate, and table likewise retain broad photographic tonal transitions rather than showing convincing graphite hatching, stroke-density modeling, or rubbed-pencil shading across the scene. The added surface texture alone does not establish pencil-rendered tonal modeling.
